message:
docs(host): the lingering guard is not about memory safety, and I said it was

Product 1, comments only. No behaviour change.

Two commits ago I wrote that a helper outliving its kill would be writing into a page the parent
had freed, and held its handles to prevent that. The reviewer pointed out the first half is wrong,
and it is. The helper opened the section itself and holds its own view, so the section lives as
long as it does; the parent's UnmapViewOfFile releases only the parent's mapping of it. Cross
process is precisely where that hazard does not exist -- which is most of the reason the capture
was moved into a process in the first place.

So the justification is corrected rather than the code. Holding the handles is still worth doing,
for a smaller and true reason: a helper that survived TerminateProcess means something is wrong in
a way nobody here understands, keeping its handle is what lets the next request notice when it
finally goes, and refusing captures in the meantime bounds the situation at one stray process
instead of one per request. That is a resource decision, and it now reads as one.

The branch is still unexercised and still says so.

Worth naming the shape of the mistake: a comment that argued for correct code with an incorrect
reason. Nothing fails, nothing looks wrong, and the next person to touch it inherits the wrong
model of why it is there. Two of the defects found earlier in this task were exactly that -- a
stale claim about WM_PRINT and a stale claim about there being one dispatcher -- and this one was
mine.
